$provenance: The shared design_id conformance corpus. ONE list of paths, exercised through BOTH implementations — crux_cxp's Dart cxpDesignIdForPath (via tool/dart-conformance/design_id_tokens.dart) and the TypeScript port in src/cxp/design-id.ts — with the two token sets asserted byte-identical by test/cxp/design-id-conformance.test.ts. Add a case here, not in the test. The 'lexical' cases name paths under a directory that cannot exist, so their tokens are machine-independent on POSIX and are committed in expected.json; the 'filesystem' cases are materialised in a fresh temp tree whose absolute path differs per run, so their tokens cannot be committed and are checked by the live cross-run plus the relational invariants the test states.

lexical.name: file-under-missing-dir
lexical.note: The not-yet-created design. Nothing on the path exists, so both sides take the pure-path fallback and hash the parent directory.

lexical.name: missing-dir-itself
lexical.note: A directory that does not exist cannot be identified as one, so the derivation takes its PARENT. This case must therefore NOT equal file-under-missing-dir — the two agree only once the directory exists. Both implementations have this property; a port that 'helpfully' guessed directory-ness from a missing trailing extension would break the join.

lexical.name: missing-dir-trailing-separator
lexical.note: Trailing separator stripped before anything else, so identical to missing-dir-itself. This is the case Node's path.normalize gets wrong on its own: it preserves the trailing slash where Dart's p.normalize removes it.

lexical.name: missing-double-separator
lexical.note: Repeated separators collapse in normalize on both sides.

lexical.name: missing-dot-segments
lexical.note: `.` and `..` are collapsed lexically before the containing directory is taken.

lexical.name: missing-parent-escape
lexical.note: `..` escapes the design folder: the token is `other`'s, not `design`'s.

lexical.name: missing-lowercase
lexical.note: Paired with missing-uppercase. On POSIX the two are DIFFERENT designs, because package:path folds case only under the Windows style — not on macOS, whose volume is usually case-insensitive but whose path style is posix. A port that folded case on darwin would silently merge two designs.

lexical.name: missing-spaces-and-unicode
lexical.note: The digest is over UTF-8 bytes on both sides; a non-ASCII folder name is where a UTF-16-vs-UTF-8 slip would show.

lexical.name: root-file
lexical.note: A file directly under the filesystem root: the containing directory is `/`, whose trailing separator must survive because it IS the root.

cases.name: dir
cases.note: The design folder itself.

cases.name: dir-trailing-separator
cases.note: Same design.

cases.name: dir-double-trailing-separator
cases.note: Same design.

cases.name: file-in-dir
cases.note: A file names its folder's design — the property the whole scheme rests on.

cases.name: other-file-in-dir
cases.note: Any file in the folder, not one privileged file.

cases.name: nested-dir
cases.note: A nested folder is its OWN design; the scheme does not walk up looking for a project marker.

cases.name: nested-file
cases.note: Belongs to the nested design, not to `design`.

cases.name: sibling-file
cases.note: Same leaf name, different folder, different design.

cases.name: dot-segments
cases.note: Collapses to the file in `design`.

cases.name: parent-escape
cases.note: Collapses to the file in `other`.

cases.name: symlinked-dir
cases.note: A symlink to the design folder resolves to the folder — statSync and Dart's typeSync both follow links, so this is identified as a directory rather than as a file.

cases.name: file-through-symlinked-dir
cases.note: Reached through the link, resolved to the real folder.

cases.name: symlinked-file
cases.note: A symlink to a file: not a directory, so the parent is taken and the link is never followed.

cases.name: missing-file-in-existing-dir
cases.note: The artifact a producer is about to write. Same design as `dir` — this is what makes the function total for a design mid-creation.

cases.name: missing-dir-in-existing-dir
cases.note: Indistinguishable from a missing file, so it resolves to `design`. Documented, not accidental.

cases.name: missing-deep
cases.note: No existing ancestor for the containing directory, so the pure-path fallback runs even though the corpus root exists.

cases.name: case-variant-dir
cases.note: Deliberately platform-dependent: on a case-insensitive volume this IS `design` and realpath(3) returns the casing as given, so the token differs from `dir`; on Linux the path does not exist at all and the token is the root's. Whatever the platform does, the two implementations must do the same thing — which is exactly what this case measures and no committed golden could.

cases.name: root-itself
cases.note: The corpus root, reached through whatever symlinks the OS puts in a temp path (on macOS /var -> /private/var), which is the symlink resolution the derivation relies on.

cases.name: relative-dot
cases.note: A relative input canonicalizes against the process working directory. The harness runs the Dart child with the same cwd, so a divergence here would be a real one.

cases.name: relative-parent
cases.note: As above, one level up.

cases.name: empty
cases.note: Normalizes to `.` on both sides — an empty path is the working directory, not an error.
